trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival — Flight AC lands at 13:00, so no morning activities scheduled. Use the morning flight time to rest and prepare.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to Old Montreal Stay (~14:00), then take a self-guided walk through Vieux-Montréal's cobblestone streets. Explore Place Jacques-Cartier, admire the Basilique Notre-Dame exterior (free outside), and soak in the historic architecture along Rue Saint-Paul. This is a perfect low-cost orientation to the neighborhood right from your doorstep.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Just for Laughs Festival Street Shows — July 15 falls right in the heart of the festival season. Catch free outdoor comedy performances and street acts along Saint-Denis and the Quartier des Spectacles. The festival atmosphere is electric and completely free to enjoy.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab something light at the airport before landing.
meals.lunch: After check-in, grab a classic Montreal-style bagel with cream cheese and smoked salmon from a nearby bakery on Rue Saint-Paul (~$6–8 CAD). A quick, authentic, and budget-friendly introduction to local food.
meals.dinner: Try La Banquise-style poutine at a casual Old Montreal spot — look for Chez Claudette or a local poutinerie near the festival area. Classic poutine (fries, cheese curds, gravy) runs ~$12–15 CAD and is the quintessential Montreal budget meal.

day_by_day.notes: Arrive refreshed and keep Day 1 light. The Just for Laughs free street shows require no tickets — just show up around the Quartier des Spectacles. Wear comfortable shoes for cobblestones. Exchange or withdraw some CAD cash as smaller food vendors may be cash-only.

day_by_day.morning: Jean-Talon Market Food Tour — Take the Metro (Orange Line, ~25 min, $3.75 CAD) up to the Jean-Talon Market, one of North America's largest open-air markets. Wander the stalls sampling Quebec cheeses, fresh seasonal berries, maple taffy, and artisan bread. Arrive by 9:00–9:30 AM when it's freshest and least crowded. Many vendors offer free tastes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Mile-Ex and Little Italy neighborhoods surrounding Jean-Talon Market on foot — browse independent shops, colorful murals, and local cafés. Head back toward the Plateau-Mont-Royal district and visit Parc La Fontaine (free), a beautiful urban park ideal for a budget picnic with market finds. Rent a pedal boat on the park lake for ~$20 CAD/hour if desired.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Quartier des Spectacles for more Just for Laughs free outdoor programming. Thursday evenings often feature larger outdoor comedy galas on the free stages. Check the official Juste pour Rire schedule for the evening's free lineup at Place des Festivals.

meals.breakfast: Eat breakfast at the market itself — a fresh croissant or pain au chocolat from a bakery stall plus a coffee (~$5–7 CAD total).
meals.lunch: Assemble a picnic from Jean-Talon Market: local cheese, baguette, fresh fruit, and a maple product of your choice. Budget ~$10–14 CAD for a generous spread eaten in Parc La Fontaine.
meals.dinner: Try a BYOB (apportez votre vin) restaurant in the Plateau district — Montreal is famous for these budget-friendly licensed spots. Resto-Végo on Rue Saint-Denis offers hearty vegetarian plates for ~$15–18 CAD. Pick up a cheap bottle of wine at a nearby SAQ (~$12 CAD) to bring along.

day_by_day.notes: Jean-Talon Market is open 7 days a week in summer, typically 7:00 AM–6:00 PM. The Metro day pass (~$11 CAD) is worth it if you plan multiple trips. Keep your market grocery spend under $15 CAD by choosing 2–3 items to sample rather than buying full quantities of everything.

day_by_day.morning: Old Montreal Street Food & History Walk — Start the morning with a deep dive into Vieux-Montréal right from your hotel. Follow Rue Saint-Paul west to east, stopping at local bakeries for fresh Montreal bagels (St-Viateur or Fairmount-style), then explore the Marché Bonsecours exterior and the Old Port waterfront. The Pointe-à-Callière archaeology museum offers a budget-friendly morning option (~$22 CAD) if history interests you, or enjoy the exterior plaza for free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or bike (BIXI bike share, ~$7 CAD for a 24-hr pass) along the Old Port waterfront to the Clock Tower Beach area. Enjoy the views of the St. Lawrence River, browse the free outdoor art installations, and relax on the waterfront. In the afternoon, head up to Mont Royal Park via the BIXI — the climb is free and the panoramic view of the city skyline from the Kondiaronk Belvedere is spectacular and costs nothing.
day_by_day.evening: Friday night at Just for Laughs is peak festival energy. The free outdoor shows on the main stages at Place des Festivals run late into the night. International comedians, street performers, and live music fill the area. Arrive by 7:00 PM to secure a good spot for the main free outdoor gala.

meals.breakfast: Fresh Montreal bagel (plain or sesame) with cream cheese from a bakery near Old Montreal — ~$3–5 CAD. Simple, iconic, and delicious.
meals.lunch: Grab a crêpe or a gyro-style wrap from a street food vendor along the Old Port (~$10–12 CAD). The waterfront area has several affordable food trucks and kiosks in summer.
meals.dinner: Pre-festival dinner at Marché 27 or a similar affordable Old Montreal café. Try a hearty soupe à l'oignon (French onion soup) and a sandwich or tartine for ~$14–17 CAD before heading to the evening shows.

day_by_day.notes: BIXI bike share is the best budget transport option for getting between Old Montreal and Mont Royal. Friday is the busiest Just for Laughs night — arrive at Place des Festivals early for free outdoor shows. Weather is warm (25°C highs), so bring water and sunscreen for the afternoon outdoor activities.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Marché Atwater, Montreal's other beloved public market, a short walk or BIXI ride from Old Montreal along the Lachine Canal. Browse local produce, artisan cheeses, charcuterie, and Québécois specialty foods. The canal-side setting is beautiful for a morning stroll. Walk or cycle along the Lachine Canal bike path (flat, scenic, and free) for a true local Saturday morning experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the Plateau-Mont-Royal neighborhood to explore independently. Visit the vibrant Rue Mont-Royal for local boutiques, street art, and café culture. Check out the free murals of the Mile End district — Montreal has one of North America's best public street art scenes. Spend a relaxed final afternoon soaking up the city's creative, multicultural energy.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening — return to the Just for Laughs Festival for the Saturday night free outdoor shows, typically the biggest and most spectacular of the week. Afterward, take a final night stroll through Vieux-Montréal, now beautifully lit, and enjoy the atmosphere of the cobblestone streets one last time before departure.

meals.breakfast: Pick up a café au lait and a butter croissant or pain aux raisins from a local boulangerie near your hotel (~$5–6 CAD). Sit outside and enjoy the Old Montreal morning quiet before the crowds arrive.
meals.lunch: Assemble another market picnic from Atwater Market along the Lachine Canal — local charcuterie, cheese, fresh bread, and seasonal fruit. Budget ~$12–15 CAD and eat canal-side on the grass.
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly on your final night with a classic Québécois meal at a casual BYOB bistro in the Plateau. Try tourtière (meat pie), maple-glazed duck, or a hearty cassoulet at a neighborhood spot. Budget ~$20–25 CAD for a main and dessert — a fitting farewell to Montreal's food culture.

day_by_day.notes: Check out time from Old Montreal Stay — confirm with the hotel if late checkout is possible to store luggage. The Lachine Canal path is flat and perfect for a leisurely BIXI ride. Saturday is the final full day, so pace yourself and prioritize the experiences that resonated most during the trip. Keep $20–30 CAD in reserve for any last-minute Metro fares or small souvenir purchases.

trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Montreal-Trudeau Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer to Old Montreal Stay hotel (~30 min by taxi or shuttle). Check in, freshen up, and orient yourself with a leisurely stroll along the cobblestone streets of Vieux-Montréal to shake off travel fatigue.
day_by_day.afternoon: Old Montreal Street Food & History Walk: Starting from your hotel, explore the historic heart of the city on foot. Stop at local bakeries for fresh Montreal-style bagels, grab a classic poutine from a neighbourhood spot, and admire landmarks like Place Jacques-Cartier and the Notre-Dame Basilica exterior. This self-guided/tour walk is perfectly accessible from your hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Old Port waterfront for the Just for Laughs Festival Street Shows — free outdoor comedy performances happening throughout the festival grounds near Vieux-Montréal. Enjoy the lively summer atmosphere, street performers, and spontaneous laughs as the sun sets over the St. Lawrence River.

meals.breakfast: Grab something light at the airport or on arrival — a coffee and pastry from a café near the hotel once you check in.
meals.lunch: During the afternoon walk, stop at Olive & Gourmando (Rue Saint-Paul Ouest) for a hearty sandwich or salad — a beloved Old Montreal institution, mid-range pricing (~$15–20 CAD).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Le Cartet (Rue McGill) — a casual yet refined market-style bistro in Old Montreal offering Quebec comfort food. Budget ~$30–45 CAD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Since your flight lands at 13:00, Day 1 is intentionally lighter. Keep luggage at the hotel and wear comfortable walking shoes. The Just for Laughs festival runs mid-July, so check the official schedule for that evening's street show locations near the Old Port.

day_by_day.morning: Jean-Talon Market Food Tour: Take the metro (Orange Line to Jean-Talon station) to one of North America's largest open-air markets. Join a guided food tour or explore independently — sample Quebec cheeses, fresh maple products, local charcuterie, seasonal fruits, and artisan preserves. Arrive early (9:00–10:00) for the best energy and freshest produce.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Plateau-Mont-Royal neighbourhood near Jean-Talon. Browse independent boutiques and street art along Avenue du Mont-Royal, then make your way to Parc La Fontaine for a relaxing afternoon picnic with market finds. Enjoy the warm 25°C weather and watch locals enjoy their summer day.
day_by_day.evening: Return toward Old Montreal and attend another evening of Just for Laughs Festival Street Shows — tonight explore the main festival hub on Rue Saint-Denis or Place des Arts for larger free outdoor stages, roaming comedians, and a buzzing crowd.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel or a nearby café — try Crew Collective & Café (Old Montreal) for coffee and a croissant in a stunning bank-turned-café setting (~$10–15 CAD).
meals.lunch: Eat at the Jean-Talon Market itself — pick up a fresh baguette, local cheese, smoked meats, and seasonal produce for an authentic Quebec picnic. Budget ~$15–20 CAD.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Damas Restaurant (Avenue de la Courtepaille, Mile End) — award-winning Syrian-Mediterranean cuisine, a local favourite. Mid-range at ~$35–50 CAD per person.

day_by_day.notes: The metro Orange Line connects Old Montreal to Jean-Talon efficiently (~25 min). Bring a reusable bag for market shopping. If it rains (30mm monthly average), the market has covered sections and the afternoon can flex to an indoor gallery or café on Rue Saint-Denis.

day_by_day.morning: Mile End Smoked Meat & Bagel Crawl: Head to the trendy Mile End neighbourhood (short metro or Bixi bike ride from downtown). Start at St-Viateur Bagel for freshly wood-fired bagels, then visit Schwartz's Deli for the legendary Montreal smoked meat sandwich — a true bucket-list food experience. Explore the neighbourhood's Jewish deli heritage and vibrant street murals.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Mount Royal Park — take the scenic trail or hop on a Bixi bike to reach the Kondiaronk Belvedere lookout for a panoramic view of the Montreal skyline. Enjoy the warm summer afternoon outdoors with locals. The park is a beloved green heart of the city and a perfect mid-trip recharge.
day_by_day.evening: Back in Old Montreal, attend the Just for Laughs Festival evening programming — Friday nights typically feature bigger headline street events and themed comedy zones. Check the festival app for special free shows near the Old Port or Quartier des Spectacles.

meals.breakfast: Bagels from St-Viateur Bagel (Mile End) with cream cheese and smoked salmon — the quintessential Montreal morning (~$8–12 CAD).
meals.lunch: Smoked meat sandwich at Schwartz's Deli (Boulevard Saint-Laurent) — a Montreal institution. Classic sandwich with coleslaw and a pickle (~$18–22 CAD).
meals.dinner: Dinner at L'Express (Rue Saint-Denis, Plateau) — a classic French-Québécois bistro with a lively atmosphere, great wine list, and dishes like steak frites and duck confit. Mid-range ~$35–50 CAD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Mile End and Mount Royal are best explored by Bixi (Montreal's bike-share system) — affordable, fun, and very local. Friday evening at Just for Laughs is one of the busiest nights, so arrive early to the festival hub to claim a good spot for outdoor shows.

day_by_day.morning: Revisit Old Montreal with fresh eyes — visit the interior of Notre-Dame Basilica (ticketed, ~$15 CAD) for its stunning neo-Gothic architecture, then walk along the Old Port waterfront. Browse the weekend artisan market at Place Jacques-Cartier where local vendors sell crafts, art, and Quebec-made goods.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final food experience: join the Montreal en Lumière Festival Experience (if overlapping with any summer edition events) or explore Quartier des Spectacles — the cultural heart of Montreal — for afternoon street performances, public art installations, and local food vendors. This area is vibrant on summer Saturdays with free programming.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Old Montreal followed by a final stroll along the illuminated waterfront. Enjoy the warm July evening, reflecting on the trip with a local craft beer or Quebec cider at a rooftop terrace bar.

meals.breakfast: Brunch at Arthurs Nosh Bar (Old Montreal area) or Olive & Gourmando — indulge in a leisurely weekend brunch with eggs, smoked salmon, and fresh-pressed juice (~$20–28 CAD).
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a food stall or café in Place Jacques-Cartier — try a crêpe, fresh fruit, or a Québécois tourtière slice from a market vendor (~$12–18 CAD).
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Garde Manger (Rue Saint-François-Xavier, Old Montreal) — Chef Chuck Hughes' beloved seafood-forward restaurant with a lively, festive atmosphere. Mid-range ~$45–60 CAD per person. Reserve in advance for Saturday evening.

day_by_day.notes: Saturday is the most vibrant day in Old Montreal and Quartier des Spectacles — expect crowds but also the best street energy. If departing on July 19, pack the night before and confirm checkout time with your hotel. The Just for Laughs Festival typically runs through the weekend, so Saturday evening may offer a grand finale street show to close out your trip on a high note.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Montreal-Trudeau Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer via private car service to your boutique hotel in Old Montreal. Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll along the cobblestone streets of Vieux-Montréal to orient yourself with the neighborhood's stunning 17th-century architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Old Montreal Street Food & History Walk: Begin your Montreal experience with a guided walk through the historic heart of the city. Stop at artisan bakeries for freshly baked Montreal-style bagels, sample rich poutine at a beloved local spot, and explore Place Jacques-Cartier buzzing with summer energy. Your guide will weave in stories of New France, merchants, and the city's layered cultural history.
day_by_day.evening: Just for Laughs Festival Street Shows: Head to the festival village (a short walk or quick ride from Old Montreal) to catch free outdoor comedy performances on the outdoor stages. Soak up the electric summer atmosphere with thousands of locals and visitors laughing under the warm July sky. Afterward, explore the festival's premium ticketed indoor shows for world-class headliner comedians.

meals.lunch: Grab a light bite upon arrival at Olive & Gourmando in Old Montreal — a beloved artisan café known for its gourmet sandwiches, fresh-baked pastries, and locally sourced ingredients. Perfect for a refined yet casual first taste of Montreal.
meals.dinner: Toqué! — Montreal's legendary fine-dining institution helmed by chef Normand Laprise. Celebrate your arrival with a tasting menu showcasing the very best of Quebec's seasonal ingredients, paired with an exceptional wine selection from their award-winning cellar. Reserve well in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Private airport transfer recommended for a seamless luxury arrival. Book Toqué! reservations months ahead as it is consistently one of Montreal's most sought-after tables. The Just for Laughs Festival runs mid-July — check the official schedule upon arrival for headliner show tickets.

day_by_day.morning: Jean-Talon Market Food Tour: Start the day with a premium guided food tour of Jean-Talon Market, one of North America's largest and most vibrant open-air markets. Sample artisan Quebec cheeses, fresh maple products, heirloom produce, charcuterie, and freshly baked goods. Your expert guide will introduce you to local producers and explain the deep agricultural traditions of Quebec. Arrive early to experience the market at its freshest and most lively.
day_by_day.afternoon: Mile End Smoked Meat & Bagel Crawl: Journey into the trendy Mile End neighborhood to explore Montreal's iconic Jewish deli culture. Visit legendary Schwartz's Deli for world-famous smoked meat, stop at St-Viateur Bagel for hand-rolled, wood-fired bagels, and browse the neighborhood's independent boutiques and street art. Mile End is also the creative heartbeat of Montreal — enjoy the bohemian atmosphere at a relaxed pace.
day_by_day.evening: Just for Laughs Festival — Premium Evening Experience: Return to the Just for Laughs Festival for a premium ticketed indoor show featuring an internationally acclaimed headliner comedian at one of the festival's main venues (e.g., Théâtre St-Denis or Salle Wilfrid-Pelletier). Enjoy VIP seating and the full production spectacle of the world's most famous comedy festival.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast at your Old Montreal boutique property, or head to Crew Collective & Café in the stunning former Royal Bank of Canada building for artisan coffee and freshly baked pastries in one of the city's most beautiful spaces.
meals.lunch: Joe Beef (or its sister restaurant Liverpool House) in Little Burgundy — a pilgrimage-worthy destination for lovers of indulgent, ingredient-driven Quebec cuisine. Known for their legendary chalkboard menu, exceptional natural wine list, and convivial atmosphere. Book ahead.
meals.dinner: Le Filet — an intimate, sophisticated seafood-focused restaurant in the Plateau-Mont-Royal area. Known for its refined small plates, creative preparations of fresh fish and shellfish, and an outstanding natural wine program. Ideal for a lighter, elegant dinner before the evening show.

day_by_day.notes: Jean-Talon Market is best enjoyed between 8:00–11:00 AM before the crowds peak. Arrange a private food tour guide for the most immersive experience. Joe Beef is one of Canada's most celebrated restaurants — reservations are essential and often require booking weeks in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Mont Royal Park & Belvedere Kondiaronk: Begin the morning with a scenic walk or private guided hike up Mont Royal, the iconic hill at the heart of the city designed by Frederick Law Olmsted. Reach the Belvedere Kondiaronk lookout for panoramic views of the Montreal skyline and the St. Lawrence River. On a warm July morning, the park is alive with locals jogging, picnicking, and playing tam-tams — a quintessential Montreal experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Plateau-Mont-Royal Neighborhood Exploration & Spa Retreat: Wander the colorful streets of the Plateau, Montreal's most characteristically local neighborhood, admiring the iconic outdoor spiral staircases, vibrant murals, and independent boutiques. In the mid-afternoon, indulge in a luxurious treatment at Bota Bota, a floating Nordic spa moored in the Old Port of Montreal. Enjoy the thermal circuit of hot baths, steam rooms, and cold plunges aboard a beautifully converted river ferry.
day_by_day.evening: Old Port Waterfront & Night Atmosphere: As the sun sets over the St. Lawrence River, stroll the Old Port promenade, which buzzes with festivals, street performers, and summer energy in July. Take in the views of the illuminated Jacques-Cartier Bridge. End the evening with cocktails at a rooftop bar overlooking the river.

meals.breakfast: Fabergé in the Plateau — a beloved neighborhood brunch institution serving creative, beautifully presented dishes with Quebec flair. Try their eggs Benedict variations or seasonal French toast with local maple syrup.
meals.lunch: Provisions — a refined yet approachable restaurant in the Plateau known for its seasonal, locally sourced menu and natural wine list. Perfect for a leisurely lunch after your morning walk.
meals.dinner: Maison Boulud at the Ritz-Carlton Montreal — Chef Daniel Boulud's Montreal outpost offers an exquisite French-inspired menu in one of the city's most elegant dining rooms. The summer terrace overlooking the hotel's rose garden is one of Montreal's most coveted dining settings. Pair your meal with selections from their world-class wine cellar.

day_by_day.notes: Book Bota Bota spa treatments in advance, especially for a Friday afternoon in peak summer season. Maison Boulud reservations at the Ritz-Carlton are essential — request the garden terrace for the ultimate summer dining experience. The Old Port is particularly vibrant on Friday evenings with the summer festival calendar in full swing.

day_by_day.morning: Marché Atwater & Canal Lachine Bike Ride: Start your final full day at Marché Atwater, a beautiful art deco covered market along the Lachine Canal. Browse local cheese mongers, butchers, florists, and specialty food vendors — pick up provisions for a gourmet picnic. Then rent premium bikes (or arrange a private guided cycling tour) and ride along the scenic Lachine Canal, a beloved green corridor through the heart of the city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Montreal Museum of Fine Arts (MBAM) — Premium Experience: Spend the afternoon at one of Canada's premier art museums. The MBAM's permanent collection spans antiquity to contemporary art, and in July there is typically a major blockbuster summer exhibition. Opt for the museum's premium guided tour for an in-depth, curated experience. The museum's architecture itself — spanning several interconnected pavilions — is a work of art.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Evening — Golden Square Mile & Downtown Montreal: Explore the Golden Square Mile, Montreal's historic enclave of Gilded Age mansions and grand architecture. Toast your final evening with cocktails at the Bar George inside the Hotel William Gray in Old Montreal — one of the city's most stylish hotel bars with a stunning rooftop terrace. End the trip with a memorable farewell dinner.

meals.breakfast: Brioche Dorée or Olive & Gourmando for a final Old Montreal morning pastry and café au lait, or enjoy a luxurious in-hotel breakfast to start the day at a relaxed pace.
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic along the Lachine Canal using artisan provisions from Marché Atwater — Quebec cheeses, charcuterie, fresh bread, seasonal fruit, and a bottle of local cider or wine. A quintessentially Montreal summer experience.
meals.dinner: Pastel — one of Montreal's most exciting contemporary fine-dining destinations, known for its innovative tasting menu that pushes the boundaries of Quebec cuisine with global influences. An intimate, design-forward space with impeccable service. The perfect celebratory farewell dinner to close a premium Montreal experience.

day_by_day.notes: The Lachine Canal bike path is flat and accessible — ideal for a leisurely morning ride. Confirm MBAM summer exhibition schedules in advance and book any premium guided tours ahead of time. Bar George rooftop is extremely popular on Saturday evenings in summer — arrive early or make a reservation. Pastel operates a tasting-menu format; book well in advance as it is one of the city's hardest reservations to secure.
